issues.issue_title: RTC init: time/date set in separate INIT sessions violates RM sequence (risk of mismatch around midnight)
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: RTC init: time/date set in separate INIT sessions violates RM sequence (risk of mismatch around midnight)
Context: repo=stm32wlxx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=low, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=11
Root cause: Hello @zudaR107, Thank you for this interesting analysis.
Fix: **Series/Device**: STM32WL (tested on STM32WLE5JCI6 / ST50H) **HAL files**: stm32wlxx_hal_rtc.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, usage_question, low, enhancement, wontfix, rtc, STM32WL, STM32WLE5JCI6, ST50H, HAL_RTC_SetTime, HAL_RTC_SetDate, RTC_EnterInitMode

Technical details:
**Series/Device**: STM32WL (tested on STM32WLE5JCI6 / ST50H) **HAL files**: stm32wlxx_hal_rtc.c — HAL_RTC_SetTime(), HAL_RTC_SetDate(), RTC_EnterInitMode(), RTC_ExitInitMode() **Summary** Current HAL sets time and date using **two consecutive INIT sessions**: each of HAL_RTC_SetTime() and HAL_RTC_SetDate() calls RTC_EnterInitMode() and RTC_ExitInitMode() separately. According to the RM, initial calendar programming must write **TR and DR within a single INIT session** (enter INIT once, program prescalers/BIN/BCDU and **both** TR & DR, set FMT, then exit). Exiting INIT between the two writes allows the calendar to tick and can produce an inconsistent (time, date) pair. **Impact** If any delay occurs between the two calls (RTOS scheduling, breakpoints, IRQs), a boundary case like setting time to 23:59:59 may yield date/time mismatch (e.g., time rolls over to 00:00 while date remains "yesterday"). **How to reproduce** Use CubeMX-generated MX_RTC_Init() that calls HAL_RTC_SetTime() then HAL_RTC_SetDate(). Add a small delay or hit a breakpoint between the two calls; check DR/TR across midnight. **Expected (per RM)** Both RTC_TR and RTC_DR are programmed **atomically** in one INIT session; counting resumes only after both are written. **Suggestion** * Provide an atomic API, e.g. HAL_RTC_SetCalendar() / HAL_RTC_SetTimeDateAtomic() that writes TR & DR within the **same** INIT session, or * Add an option/flag to keep INIT asserted across SetTime+SetDate, and * Update CubeMX templates to use the atomic path during initial calendar setup. **Workaround** Write TR and DR in a single custom INIT session (or temporarily disable scheduler/IRQs between the two HAL calls): c __HAL_RTC_WRITEPROTECTION_DISABLE(&hrtc); if (RTC_EnterInitMode(&hrtc) == HAL_OK) { /* build TR/DR values as in HAL */ WRITE_REG(RTC->TR, tr); WRITE_REG(RTC->DR, dr); RTC_ExitInitMode(&hrtc); } __HAL_RTC_WRITEPROTECTION_ENABLE(&hrtc); **Question** Is the current two-session behavior intentional? If not, please consider the fix above and clarify the intended sequence in HAL docs/comments.

Key comments:
Hello @zudaR107, Thank you for this interesting analysis. The current implementation is intentional to allow some flexibility when configuring the RTC calendar. Regarding the case you described, I understand it might happen. However, it seems very unlikely. Indeed, the RTC is normally configured to increment **once per second**. This is enough for both date and time to be set correctly without the time register rolling over, considering a CPU frequency of up to **48 MHz** in the case of a STM32WL microcontroller. You also mentioned placing a breakpoint or calling a delay function. In these cases, the issue is triggered intentionally. This is rather a debugging practice and is very unlikely to occur in real-world applications. But even if we suppose it might happen due to an interrupt, the recommendation in such a case is to set the date **before** the time. Hello @ALABSTM, Thank you for your detailed reply. Let me clarify my concern a bit more concretely. We are considering the following situation: we first set the time to 23:59:59, and then we set the date. If both operations complete within one second, I fully agree that the result will be consistent. However, in a real

Problem: Wrong bit checks in `FLASH_FlushCaches` (stm32wlxx_hal_driver)
Context: repo=stm32wlxx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=10
Root cause: Hello @zudaR107, Yes, you are right, but we will fix it by replace 1U by bits masks FLASH_ACR_DCEN and FLASH_ACR_ICEN.
Fix: # Wrong bit checks in FLASH_FlushCaches (stm32wlxx_hal_driver) **Repository:** STMicroelectronics/stm32wlxx-hal-driver **File:** Src/stm32wlxx_hal_flash_ex.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, spotted before customer, flash, FLASH_FlushCaches, READ_BIT, ACR, FLASH_ACR_ICEN, FLASH_ACR_DCEN

Technical details:
# Wrong bit checks in FLASH_FlushCaches (stm32wlxx_hal_driver) **Repository:** STMicroelectronics/stm32wlxx-hal-driver **File:** Src/stm32wlxx_hal_flash_ex.c **Function:** FLASH_FlushCaches() ## Summary In FLASH_FlushCaches, the code checks cache-enable bits with == 1U: c if (READ_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_ICEN) == 1U) { __HAL_FLASH_INSTRUCTION_CACHE_DISABLE(); __HAL_FLASH_INSTRUCTION_CACHE_RESET(); __HAL_FLASH_INSTRUCTION_CACHE_ENABLE(); } ... if (READ_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_DCEN) == 1U) { __HAL_FLASH_DATA_CACHE_DISABLE(); __HAL_FLASH_DATA_CACHE_RESET(); __HAL_FLASH_DATA_CACHE_ENABLE(); } However, FLASH_ACR_ICEN and FLASH_ACR_DCEN are **bit masks** defined as (0x1UL << 9) and (0x1UL << 10) respectively. READ_BIT(...) returns either 0 or the **mask value** (e.g., 0x200, 0x400), so comparing the result to 1U is always false. As a result, caches are never flushed even when enabled. ## Expected behavior Use a non-zero test for these mask bits: c if (READ_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_ICEN) != 0U) { __HAL_FLASH_INSTRUCTION_CACHE_DISABLE(); __HAL_FLASH_INSTRUCTION_CACHE_RESET(); __HAL_FLASH_INSTRUCTION_CACHE_ENABLE(); } #ifndef CORE_CM0PLUS if (READ_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_DCEN) != 0U) { __HAL_FLASH_DATA_CACHE_DISABLE(); __HAL_FLASH_DATA_CACHE_RESET(); __HAL_FLASH_DATA_CACHE_ENABLE(); } #endif ## Why this matters If the instruction/data caches remain unflushed after erase/program operations, software may execute or read stale content from Flash, causing hard-to-diagnose runtime issues. ## Environment * Series: **STM32WLxx** (observed on STM32WLE5JCI6) * Package: stm32wlxx_hal_driver (current main, Nov 2025) ## Additional notes This pattern might exist in other STM32Cube HAL repositories—worth a quick grep for == 1U checks against mask-type bit defines. ## Suggested fix Replace both comparisons with != 0U as shown above.

Key comments:
Hello @zudaR107, Yes, you are right, but we will fix it by replace 1U by bits masks FLASH_ACR_DCEN and FLASH_ACR_ICEN. Thank you for this heads-up. I'll log an internal tracker. BR, Mohamed. ST Internal Reference: 218655

issues.issue_title: [WL][HAL][ADC] Calibration may fail / internal error with slow ADC clock (HSI + async DIV64). Need to wait for ADRDY before writing calibration factor and disabling ADC.
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: [WL][HAL][ADC] Calibration may fail / internal error with slow ADC clock (HSI + async DIV64). Need to wait for ADRDY before writing calibration factor and disabling ADC.
Context: repo=stm32wlxx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=ADC, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=7
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 129648 ST Internal Reference: 219975 ST Internal Reference: 219976 Hello @zudaR107, Thank you for the report, The issue about check ADRDY will be fixed in next release.
Fix: ## Summary When running HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start() on STM32WL with **HSI (16 MHz)** and **ADC asynchronous prescaler = DIV64** (i.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, ADC, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, spotted before customer, HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start, STM32WL, HSI, DIV64, HAL_ADC_ERROR_INTERNAL

Technical details:
## Summary When running HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start() on STM32WL with **HSI (16 MHz)** and **ADC asynchronous prescaler = DIV64** (i.e. **fADC ≈ 250 kHz**), ADC calibration intermittently fails with HAL_ADC_ERROR_INTERNAL and the function may return from the **disable-wait** loop with an error. Root cause: after averaging the calibration factor, the HAL **immediately** programs the factor and disables the ADC, but **does not wait for ADRDY** (ADC ready) after enabling. With a **slow fADC** this violates the enable/disable sequence timing, and the peripheral may not be ready when ADDIS is requested. Additionally, on the error path that times out waiting for ADC disable, there is a missing __HAL_UNLOCK(hadc) before returning, which can leave the handle locked. --- ## Environment * **MCU**: **STM32WLE5JCI6** * **Board**: **ST50H** * **Cube FW package**: STM32Cube_FW_WL_V1.3.1 * **Toolchain**: **CubeMX v6.15.0 / GCC v14.2.0 / Makefile** * **Clocking relevant to ADC**: * ADC clock source: **HSI 16 MHz** (RCC_ADCCLKSOURCE_HSI) * Asynchronous prescaler: **ADC_CLOCK_ASYNC_DIV64** ⇒ **fADC ≈ 250 kHz** * (When using **DIV1**, the issue does **not** reproduce.) --- ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure ADC: * RCC_ADCCLKSOURCE_HSI (16 MHz), * ADC_CLOCK_ASYNC_DIV64, * single conversion, software trigger, * DMA enabled in CFGR1 (HAL temporarily clears it during calibration). 2. Initialize and call calibration **before** starting any conversions / scheduler: c MX_ADC_Init(); // hadc.Init.ClockPrescaler = ADC_CLOCK_ASYNC_DIV64 HAL_ADC_Stop(&hadc); HAL_StatusTypeDef st = HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start(&hadc); 3. Observe: st != HAL_OK, HAL_ADC_GetError(&hadc) returns HAL_ADC_ERROR_INTERNAL. Sometimes it times out in the “wait until ADC disabled” section. > Workaround observed: set ADC prescaler to **DIV1** (fADC = 16 MHz) → no issue. --- ## Expected Behavior HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start() should reliably: * finish calibration, * **enable** the ADC, * **wait until ADC is ready** (ADRDY asserted, tSTAB satisfied), * write the averaged calibration factor (with ADEN=1, ADSTART=0), * **disable** the ADC, and return HAL_OK. --- ## Actual Behavior With **slow fADC** (e.g., DIV64), the function sometimes: * returns HAL_ERROR with HAL_ADC_ERROR_INTERNAL, * times out waiting for ADC to disable, * and (secondary issue) may leave the handle **locked** on that error path. --- ## Root Cause Analysis * Current HAL sequence after averaging 8 calibration runs: 1. LL_ADC_Enable() 2. **immediately** LL_ADC_SetCalibrationFactor() 3. LL_ADC_Disable() 4. wait until LL_ADC_IsEnabled()==0 * The RM for STM32WL requires waiting for **ADRDY** after setting **ADEN** (ADC enable sequence). With **low fADC**, issuing register writes and ADDIS before ADRDY can cause internal errors/timeout. * Error branch that handles “disable timeout” misses __HAL_UNLOCK(hadc) before return HAL_ERROR;. --- ## Proposed Fix Insert an **enable-and-wait-for-ADRDY** step **before** writing the calibration factor, then disable as usual. Add a small timeout for the ADRDY wait. Also ensure __HAL_UNLOCK(hadc) on all early returns. Illustrative patch (logic, not a full diff): c /* ... after computing calibration_factor_accumulated ... */ /* Apply calibration factor safely: follow ADC enable sequence */ LL_ADC_ClearFlag_ADRDY(hadc->Instance); LL_ADC_Enable(hadc->Instance); /* Wait for ADC ready (tSTAB), bounded by a short timeout */ uint32_t tickstart_local = HAL_GetTick(); while (LL_ADC_IsActiveFlag_ADRDY(hadc->Instance) == 0UL) { if ((HAL_GetTick() - tickstart_local) > ADC_STAB_TIMEOUT_MS) /* e.g. 2–5 ms */ { /* Update state and error code */ ADC_STATE_CLR_SET(hadc->State, HAL_ADC_STATE_BUSY_INTERNAL, HAL_ADC_STATE_ERROR_INTERNAL); SET_BIT(hadc->ErrorCode, HAL_ADC_ERROR_INTERNAL); __HAL_UNLOCK(hadc); return HAL_ERROR; } } /* ADEN=1, ADSTART=0: now program the averaged factor */ LL_ADC_SetCalibrationFactor(hadc->Instance, calibration_factor_accumulated); /* Then disable and wait as in the current code */ LL_ADC_Disable(hadc->Instance); /* On the later 'disable timeout' branch, also add __HAL_UNLOCK(hadc) before returning */ Notes: * ADC_STAB_TIMEOUT_MS can be a new internal define (e.g. **2–5 ms**). * No public API change; negligible time cost; robust for **slow fADC** configurations. --- ## Validation Tested on **ST50H with STM32WLE5JCI6**: * HSI 16 MHz + ADC_CLOCK_ASYNC_DIV64 (≈250 kHz): **PASS** with fix, no internal errors. * HSI 16 MHz + ADC_CLOCK_ASYNC_DIV1: **PASS** (both original and fixed code). Calibration invoked: * **Before** RTOS scheduler start → **PASS** --- ## Secondary Issue (handle lock on error path) In the branch handling “disable timeout”, please add __HAL_UNLOCK(hadc) before return HAL_ERROR;, mirroring the earlier error branch. Without it, the handle may remain locked and affect other tasks/peripherals. --- ## Additional Context The issue disappears with a faster fADC (e.g., DIV1), which aligns with a timing-sequence dependency rather than application misuse. The proposed change follows the documented ADC enable sequence and should be safe across STM32WL variants. Thanks!

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 129648 ST Internal Reference: 219975 ST Internal Reference: 219976 Hello @zudaR107, Thank you for the report, The issue about check ADRDY will be fixed in next release. will be fixed by using a delay between ADDIS and ADENA Case flag "ADRDY" not required: - ADC calibration (done when ADC disabled) - ADC calibration factors set/get Please refer to the Reference Manual, particularly the "Calibration Factor Forcing Software Procedure" section, which does not specify any condition on ADRDY=1. Flag ADRDY is set when kernel clock is present, used to clock ADC sampling and conversion. Calibration factors management is a digital operation, not requiring this clock. BR, Mohamed. Hello, @MKISTM. Thanks for the work! Hello @zudaR107, Issue fixed in the frame of release **1.4.0**, adding a delay, as explained by @MKISTM, rather than according to what you suggested. Thank you again for your report and for the suggested fix. Hello @zudaR107, About secondary issue (add __HAL_UNLOCK(hadc) before return HAL_ERROR;) will be fixed in next release. We will keep you informed. BR, Mohamed Chaker Fixed in commit 503646116743f3e23ddf17c9d91f1947fe40f0b7

issues.issue_title: Why is LL_GPIO_SetPinMode called twice in LL_GPIO_Init?
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Why is LL_GPIO_SetPinMode called twice in LL_GPIO_Init?
Context: repo=stm32wlxx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=UART, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=6
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 182334 Fixed in : 5eda2310f3bad3778ca5424b9f15b3693219eed1
Fix: I was looking at the LL_GPIO_Init function and I noticed the function LL_GPIO_SetPinMode is called twice in this function.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, UART, bug_report, medium, bug, gpio, LL_GPIO_Init, LL_GPIO_SetPinMode, PA2, LPUART1_TX

Technical details:
I was looking at the LL_GPIO_Init function and I noticed the function LL_GPIO_SetPinMode is called twice in this function. The first time is near the beginning of the function on line 178: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32wlxx_hal_driver/blob/d25d454a7b7120d99d4736066b3d0cbe5f1734a7/Src/stm32wlxx_ll_gpio.c#L178 The second time is at the end of the function on line 215: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32wlxx_hal_driver/blob/d25d454a7b7120d99d4736066b3d0cbe5f1734a7/Src/stm32wlxx_ll_gpio.c#L215 By calling LL_GPIO_SetPinMode before the various GPIO parameters are configured, it can cause unexpected behavior on the pins. I was configuring port PA2 as LPUART1_TX, and it was unexpectedly outputting a byte over UART when being configured. Removing the LL_GPIO_SetPinMode on line 178 and only calling it on line 215 fixed this bug. Unless there is some reason to call this function twice, I believe this is a bug.

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 182334 Fixed in : 5eda2310f3bad3778ca5424b9f15b3693219eed1
